# The appointments Tiāndì made — and who is keeping them

The mistake is reading myths as entertainment. Tiāndì's cycle reads more like a charter — each story assigning a duty the modern world still pays for.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Tiāndì
- **Pantheon:** Chinese
- **Domain of influence:** Cosmology, Heaven and Earth, Order
- **Pattern seats:** 5
- **Sectors touched:** Society & Spirit · Home & Lifestyle · Energy & Natural World · Health & Wellbeing · Culture & Entertainment
- **Strongest seat:** Philosophy, Ethics & Standards
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 243 of 271

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Philosophy, Ethics & Standards — through *Pangu Separates Heaven and Earth*

In the best-known Chinese creation myth, Pangu grows inside a cosmic egg for eighteen thousand years.  When he awakens, he pushes the heavy earth downward and the light heaven upward, growing taller each day.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Heaven and earth as one ethical cosmos.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Architecture & Spatial Design — through *The Son of Heaven at the Altars*

The emperor's most sacred duty was to sacrifice to Heaven at the winter solstice and to Earth at the summer solstice.  The Temple of Heaven in Beijing is the surviving monument to this rite.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Round altar, square terrace; the dyad built in stone and feng shui's first diagram.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Environmental & Climate Services — through *Heaven, Earth, and the Ten Thousand Things*

The Dàodéjīng says that the Dao gives birth to One, One gives birth to Two, Two gives birth to Three, and Three gives birth to the ten thousand things.  In many readings, the Two is the dyad of heaven and earth, the first differentiation from which all phenomena arise.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Heaven and Earth as one natural order; ecology as cosmology.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Healthcare, Pharma & Medicine — through *Pangu Separates Heaven and Earth*

In the best-known Chinese creation myth, Pangu grows inside a cosmic egg for eighteen thousand years.  When he awakens, he pushes the heavy earth downward and the light heaven upward, growing taller each day.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Harmony of heaven, earth, and humanity is the frame of traditional Chinese medicine.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Tiāndì is not a mythic protagonist but the setting within which Chinese myths unfold. Its stories are cosmogonic and ritual rather than heroic.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

Skeptical? Good — the system is built for you. Every seat in this file carries its why-line and its weight, the full derivation is public at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/), and the challenge process is part of the design. Falsifiable is not a posture here; it is the mechanism.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in philosophy, ethics & standards, architecture & spatial design, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/tiandi/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
